summary: At just 6.5 square miles, Los Altos packs a median home value that exceeds $2 million while sitting barely four miles from the foothills of the Santa Cruz Mountains — meaning evening walks along local trails can end with unobstructed sunset light spilling over the western ridgeline, a geographic perk that most of Silicon Valley's flatter, denser cities simply can't match. The city functions largely as a bedroom community; there is no major corporate campus within its borders, yet the headquarters of Google, Apple, and dozens of mid-stage startups sit within a fifteen-minute drive, so switching employers rarely requires switching commutes. That proximity helps explain a median household income above $250,000, but even at that level the home-price-to-income ratio lands around 8:1 — roughly double what conventional lending guidelines consider comfortable. Downtown is a compact, walkable stretch anchored by independent restaurants, a weekly farmers' market, and local coffee shops rather than national chains, giving it a village-scale rhythm that contrasts sharply with the wealth the numbers imply. With 9.4 hours of average daily sunshine and highs that hover near 69°F year-round, the climate rarely forces anyone indoors, yet the streets grow conspicuously quiet after dinner. Los Altos is essentially a small town that happens to sit at the economic epicenter of the global tech industry — and the tension between those two identities defines almost every tradeoff of living there.
